name: com.visdenda/free
title: Visdenda Free MCP
description: Anonymous SEO MCP: crawler directory, site audit, cited knowledge search. No API key.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search the AI crawler directory (69 crawlers across 26 providers), active audit rules, and the public Google update radar. Returns at most 10 entries, each with an id, title and canonical URL. Call search first, then fetch with one of the returned ids. Read-only; no external network request.

query.description: Free-text query matched against titles, summaries and crawler tokens

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Read one public SEO reference by the id returned from search: an AI crawler record, an active audit rule's public summary and official source, or a public radar update. Returns the text we publish for that reference, its canonical URL and metadata for citation. Read-only; no external network request. Only ids returned by search are accepted; arbitrary URLs are rejected.

id.description: Reference id from search, e.g. crawler:gptbot, rule:<id> or radar:<slug>

tools.name: visdenda_search_ai_crawlers
tools.description: Search 69 AI crawlers across 26 providers by name, provider, robots token, user-agent substring, or category. Returns each crawler's canonical agent name, vendor, category, robots token, official sources and review date. Use this first when the user asks which AI bots exist, which vendor runs a bot, or what token to put in robots.txt. No network request.

query.description: Free-text match on provider, agent, robots token, slug or user-agent

tools.name: visdenda_get_ai_crawler
tools.description: Read the full directory record for one crawler, selected by slug, canonical agent name, or a user-agent string. Returns vendor, category, description, robots token, user-agent needles, rDNS suffixes, published IP-range URLs, static CIDR blocks, official sources and review date. Use after search when the user needs the details or a citation. No network request.

inputSchema.description: Provide exactly one of slug, agent, or userAgent

tools.name: visdenda_match_user_agent
tools.description: Given a raw user-agent or log line, return the AI/search crawlers it belongs to, ranked by exact token, prefix and substring matches. Use this when the user pastes a log entry or asks 'which bot is this?'. No network request.

userAgent.description: Raw user-agent or a log line containing one

tools.name: visdenda_check_crawler_access
tools.description: Fetch a public URL's robots.txt once and evaluate it for specific crawlers (default: every crawler in the directory). Returns allowed/blocked per crawler, whether a matching group exists, the deciding Allow/Disallow rule, crawl-delay, and sitemap pointers. Pass paths to evaluate additional same-origin paths against the same rules (no extra request). Use when the user asks 'can GPTBot read this page?', 'is ClaudeBot blocked?', or 'which AI bots can crawl my site?'. One robots.txt request; optional probe adds one page request per path as the chosen crawler's user-agent, and probeUserAgent lets you test a specific (or forged) UA.

url.description: Public http(s) URL; only its origin's robots.txt is read

crawlers.description: Optional robots tokens or agent names (default: every directory entry). Unknown names are reported as unmatched.

paths.description: Optional extra paths on the same origin as url, evaluated against the same robots.txt rules (no extra request).

probe.description: Optional. With exactly one crawler, also request the page as that crawler's user-agent to detect CDN/WAF blocks. With paths, each path is probed once.

probeUserAgent.description: Optional custom User-Agent for the probe (requires probe=true), e.g. a forged crawler string found in logs.

tools.name: visdenda_verify_crawler_ip
tools.description: Check whether an IP belongs to a named AI crawler. Pass agent (slug, agent name or robots token) to test that crawler's official ranges; omit it to try static CIDR blocks first, then reverse DNS and the crawlers whose rDNS suffixes match. Returns matched/mismatch/unavailable/not-checked plus the CIDR and rDNS evidence. Use when the user pastes a log entry and asks whether the bot is genuine. One network call; fails soft on DNS/range errors.

agent.description: Optional crawler slug, agent name or robots token

tools.name: visdenda_audit_site
tools.description: Audit one public URL or site origin and return findings that each carry a concrete fix. focus=full (default) runs the public one-page scan (20+ checks: meta, canonical, robots, sitemap, llms.txt, schema, hreflang, redirects, agent discovery) and returns a grade, every failing/warning finding and a seven-day report URL; it consumes one free scan (3/day/IP). focus=signals checks canonical, noindex, meta, hreflang and structured data; focus=agent runs up to eight agent-readiness probes with a 0–100 score; focus=mcp checks the MCP server card, OAuth discovery, auth.md and the A2A card; focus=robots, sitemap and llms run only that single check. The focused modes do not consume the scan quota. Pass updateId (full) to attach a public radar update's checks, and compareTo with a previous scanId (full) to get added, resolved and persisting findings plus the score delta. Use this instead of asking the user to run several separate checks.

url.description: Public http(s) URL or site origin

focus.description: full = complete page scan (scan quota); signals = five page signals; agent = up to eight readiness probes; mcp = MCP/OAuth discovery; robots, sitemap, llms = one focused check. Default full.

checks.description: focus=agent only: optional readiness probe ids (default: the eight cheap probes).

includeFull.description: focus=llms only: also probe /llms-full.txt (adds one network request).

updateId.description: focus=full only: public radar update id or slug to attach its checks (optional).

compareTo.description: focus=full only: scanId from a previous full audit of the same URL. Adds compare.added/resolved/persisting and scoreDelta.

tools.name: visdenda_get_agent_skill
tools.description: Load the ai-crawler-readiness skill before the first free check. Use when an agent connects to this free MCP server and needs the access -> audit -> compare loop, the free-tool order and the free-tier limits instead of a generic SEO checklist. Returns the exact SKILL.md markdown, version, canonical URL and task references. No siteId, no network; safe to call once per session.

name.description: Skill to load; only ai-crawler-readiness is available on the free server.

tools.name: visdenda_connect_account
tools.description: Start a self-service agent registration: given the user's email and optional scopes, return a claim URL, a six-digit code and a claim token. The user opens the URL, signs in and approves scopes; the agent then polls /v1/oauth2/token with the claim token to receive a one-hour access token for the account MCP server. Use when the user wants to keep results, monitor a site, or read Search Console data (an audit result's nextActions links here). Creates a pending registration, no site changes.

email.description: The account owner's email (must match the account they sign in with)
